title: CLCON/197/2004 of PUSHPENDRA SINGH Vs DINESH CHANDRA UNIYAL and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Contempt No. 197 of 2004
Pushpendra Singh S/O Shri Mukhram Singh, R/O Village
Sabalgarh, P.O. Nagaal Saitkari, District Bijnore U.P..
...... Petitioner.
Versus
Shri Dinesh Chandra Uniyal, Divisional Sales Manager,
Uttaranchal Forest Corporation, Kotdwar, District Pauri Garhwal
and two others. (Contemnors)
... Respondents.
 Sri Jitendra Chaudhary, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Sri V.K.Bist, Senior Advocate, with Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, learned counsel for the
respondents.
Date May 08, 2008.
Hon'ble B.S.Verma, J.
 Heard Sri Jitendra Chaudhary, learned counsel for the
applicant-petitioner and Sri V.K.Bist, Senior Advocate, with Sri
Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, learned counsel for the respondents and
perused the record.
 This contempt petition has been filed to punish the
respondents for willful defiance of the judgment and orders dated
24-9-2003 passed by this Court in Writ Petition No. 856 of 2003,
Khoob Singyh and others Vs. Uttaranchal Forest Development
Corporation and others.
 This Court by the order dated 24-9-2003 has issued
writ of mandamus directing the respondents to reinstate the
petitioners with continuity of service.
 So far as the reinstatement of the petitioner with
continuity of service is concerned, the petitioner has already been
given appointment as is evident from Annexure No.1 to counter
affidavit dated 3-01-2008 filed by the opposite parties.

2
 Sri V.K.Bist, Senior Advocate with Ms. S.Miyan
appearing on behalf of the opposite parties-Uttaranchal Forest
Development Corporation has urged that the opposite parties may
be allowed reasonable time to make payment of back wages to the
petitioners.
 In the circumstances of the case, the contempt petition
is dismissed. Notices issues to the respondents are discharged. It is
provided that if the back wages are not paid to the respondents
within reasonable time, the petitioner may file fresh contempt
petition against the respondents.
All pending applications stand disposed of.
